newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends mixed ahead of GCA stock report.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends mixed ahead of GCA stock report.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures ended mixed Monday, with prices retracing from session lows after a round of speculative shortcovering, traders said.

They said higher-than-expected USDA world production figures released late Friday prompted a bout of local and commission house selling, which drove most-active September to a session low of 175.00 cents a lb.
September arabicas closed at 181.60 cents, down 1.15 cents but just shy of the day's high of 182.00 cents. Spot July rose 0.80 cent to 196.50, while the back months finished up 1.00 to down 1.30.
The July/September switch widened to 14.90 cents at the close from 12.95 on Friday.
Coffee prices headed lower at the outset, defying pre-opening expectations, as traders absorbed the bi-annual world green coffee production estimate put out by the USDA late Friday.
"Specs sold initially on the USDA report, but it did not follow-through and they bought it back," said one trader. "They had sold it ahead of the news on the perception the figures would be bearish."

The USDA estimated that Brazil's 1997/98 coffee crop could reach 28 million 60-kg bags, up from a revised 27.5 million in 1996/97. USDA pegged world 1997/98 production at 103.7 million versus 100.7 million in 1996/97.
Traders from producing countries criticized the USDA estimates, which they said differed sharply from their own forecasts.

Monday, Brazil's ambassador in London, Rubens Barbosa, said his government was staying with its estimate of Brazilian 1997/98 coffee output around 22 million (60 kg) bags. Early trade estimates from Brazil put next season's crop at anywhere from 18 to 25 million 60-kg bags.
New York traders now await the monthly U.S. consumer coffee stock data for direction. The Green Coffee Association of New York will release its May inventory data today at 1500 EDT/1900 GMT.

Most industry participants expected aggressive shipments by producers to increase stocks in the U.S. by some 150,000-250,000 bags in May, although estimates ranged widely from a 25,000-bag increase to a 400,000-bag increase.

Last month, GCA reported U.S. consumer coffee stocks rose by 198,000 bags in April, to 1,855,000 bags. In May 1996, green coffee stowed in U.S. warehouses stood at 2,271,000 bags, down 25,000 from the previous month.
Volume on Monday reached an estimated 8,651 lots, traders said.
